faq.q: What is the agentic web?
faq.a: The agentic web is the machine-facing layer of a website. It presents the same business information as structured, readable data so AI assistants and agentic browsers can retrieve it, cite it and act on it without parsing a page built for human eyes.

faq.q: How is this different from SEO or GEO?
faq.a: SEO and GEO influence whether you are found and recommended. The agentic web decides what an agent can actually read and do once it arrives. They are complementary: visibility brings the agent, the agentic layer serves it.

faq.q: Do we need to rebuild our website?
faq.a: No. The agentic layer is added alongside your existing site. Your human website stays exactly as it is; we build a parallel machine-readable layer on the same domain.

faq.q: How long does an agentic web build take?
faq.a: A standard build runs about three weeks from audit to verified deployment. Larger sites with multiple markets or product catalogues take longer, mostly in data mapping.

faq.q: Why does it need monthly upkeep?
faq.a: Your website keeps changing, new crawlers and browser agents keep arriving, and the specifications themselves are still moving. Without upkeep the layer drifts out of sync and agents answer from stale data.

faq.q: How do you measure whether it worked?
faq.a: Four measures: the Lighthouse agentic browsing category, how well leading models describe your business when asked, agent and crawler traffic in your logs, and citation appearances in AI answers.

faq.q: What’s the difference between YouTube ads and a YouTube marketing strategy?
faq.a: YouTube ads generate views while your budget is active — when it stops, visibility stops. A YouTube marketing strategy builds organic discovery through search-optimised content, channel architecture, and playlist structure. The goal is content that compounds in value over time — reaching buyers through YouTube Search, Suggested Videos, and AI platforms without ongoing media spend per view. Both have a role, but most B2B companies are 100% dependent on paid. We change that ratio.

faq.q: Do we need to create a lot of new videos to see results?
faq.a: Not necessarily — and often not at all in Month 1. The highest-impact improvements almost always come from optimising what already exists: rewriting metadata, adding chapter structure, adjusting visibility settings, reorganising channel architecture, and building playlists. Most companies have a video library that significantly underperforms its potential. We unlock that first, then build a content strategy around proven demand.

faq.q: Is YouTube actually relevant for B2B companies in industrial or technical sectors?
faq.a: Especially so. Technical buyers actively use YouTube to understand how products work, compare specifications, and validate decisions before involving procurement. Categories like industrial equipment, construction machinery, logistics software, enterprise technology, and professional services all have genuine search demand on YouTube. The opportunity is large precisely because most B2B companies in these sectors have not yet invested in organic YouTube strategy — which means first movers will compound their advantage.

faq.q: What is the difference between SEO and GEO?
faq.a: SEO (Search Engine Optimization) focuses on ranking in traditional search engines like Google — getting your page to appear at the top of a results page. GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) focuses on getting your brand cited and recommended within AI-generated answers from tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. The key difference: in SEO you earn a position in a list. In GEO you earn a mention within a conversational answer. The signals that drive each are related but distinct — GEO places greater weight on entity authority, citation across trusted sources, and content that answers questions comprehensively.

faq.q: What is Generative Engine Optimization?
faq.a: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the practice of structuring your brand’s digital presence so that AI language models and search engines — like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google’s AI Overviews — are more likely to reference, cite, and recommend your brand when users ask relevant questions. It involves optimizing content for how LLMs crawl and process information, building entity authority across the web, and ensuring your brand is clearly associated with the topics and problems your customers are asking AI about.

faq.q: Is GEO replacing SEO?
faq.a: Not replacing — but fundamentally reshaping. Traditional SEO remains important, especially for transactional queries and local search. But the share of research and discovery happening through AI search is growing rapidly, particularly in B2B contexts where buyers use tools like ChatGPT to evaluate vendors before ever visiting a website. The smartest approach is to treat GEO and SEO as complementary disciplines. Many of the foundations — strong content, authoritative backlinks, technical health — benefit both. GEO adds a new layer: entity building, AI citation optimization, and prompt-level visibility tracking.

faq.q: What does the SEMrush Enterprise AIO partnership mean for me as a client?
faq.a: As the Nordics’ first SEMrush Enterprise AIO Partner, GO MO has access to the largest LLM prompt tracking database available — 213M+ real prompts monitored globally across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, and Meta AI. This means every audit and strategy we deliver is grounded in actual data about how AI engines are answering questions in your industry. Most agencies offering GEO services are working from hypothesis. We’re working from measurement. Your visibility benchmark, competitor gaps, and content priorities are all backed by real AI search data that other Nordic agencies simply don’t have access to.

faq.q: What is the Mini GEO Audit and what do I get?
faq.a: The Mini GEO Audit is a free, no-commitment snapshot of your brand’s current AI search visibility. We check how your brand appears — or doesn’t — across ChatGPT and Perplexity for your core topic areas, and deliver a 1-page summary within 48 hours. It’s the fastest way to understand your starting point before committing to a full GEO strategy. There’s no pitch, no obligation — just a clear picture of where you stand today. Request your free Mini Audit here.

faq.q: Are these designs fully AI-generated?
faq.a: Not entirely. We use Generative AI to speed up and scale the creative process, but visual is reviewed, refined, and finalized by our experts to ensure quality and brand alignment.

faq.q: How does AI improve the design process?

faq.q: What is Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)?
faq.a: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the practice of optimizing your brand’s digital presence so it appears in responses generated by LLMs and AI systems such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. GEO focuses on making your content extractable, trustworthy, and widely validated so AI systems can confidently reference and recommend it when answering user questions.

faq.q: How is GEO different from traditional SEO?
faq.a: SEO focuses on helping websites rank in search engine results pages. GEO builds on that foundation by ensuring your content can also be understood, synthesized, and cited by AI systems that generate answers directly for users. In practice, GEO expands optimization beyond search engines to include AI models, AI search tools, and emerging agent-driven discovery systems.

faq.q: Does GEO replace SEO?
faq.a: No. SEO remains the first step to building digital visibility. Search engines are still a primary source of information for both users and AI systems. GEO builds on strong SEO foundations by making your content easier for AI systems to interpret, extract, and reference in generated answers. Organizations with strong SEO often have a significant advantage when expanding into GEO.
